projects.projectName: Premera Blue Cross - AI Platform Build - Servicing

riskDescription.context: The client selected the organization based on proven AI expertise and expects proactive AI-driven recommendations and value-added insights. CSAT dimension is Red and RISK-802 (Major/Possible/High) is open in EMS, noting delivered code has not consistently reflected expected AI expertise and communication gaps have reduced confidence in offshore contributions.
riskDescription.condition: Client perception of offshore AI competency may continue to decline if proactive solutioning and architectural contributions are not demonstrated consistently.
riskDescription.consequence: Increased scrutiny and escalations could lead to lower stakeholder satisfaction, reluctance to approve future work, and potential impact to account growth and project continuity.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Conduct weekly solution demonstrations and architectural code walkthroughs with client stakeholders to showcase offshore AI capabilities and technical depth.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Upon client escalation or CSAT score drop below threshold, activate executive sponsor engagement and deploy onshore AI SME to lead client-facing technical sessions within 48 hours.

riskDescription.context: Quality dimension is Amber in EMS and RISK-801 (Major/Possible/High) is open, noting code quality concerns raised by client based on PR comments. Biweekly CES Reports (28 May, 21 May 2026) document gap in alignment between vendors and process understanding.
riskDescription.condition: Vendor alignment gaps and mid-sprint dependency changes may persist despite stringent code review measures, leading to recurring quality perception issues.
riskDescription.consequence: Team morale and client rapport could be further impacted, weakening trust in delivery quality and increasing risk of escalation.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Implement mandatory internal draft PR reviews before vendor submission and conduct bi-weekly cross-vendor quality alignment sessions with shared coding standards documentation.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: When quality concerns are raised by client, convene vendor alignment meeting within 24 hours and deploy circle QA lead to audit code samples and provide remediation plan within 72 hours.

riskDescription.context: Talent dimension is Amber in EMS. Biweekly CES Reports (14 May, 07 May 2026) document internal talent issue with UI engineer requiring replacement, and design ownership change to D365 team after resource onboarding.
riskDescription.condition: Replacement ramp-up may take longer than expected or scope alignment discussions may not identify sufficient work allocation for React engineer.
riskDescription.consequence: Sprint capacity could be constrained and deliverables may continue to be managed internally under stress, affecting team productivity and delivery pace.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Coordinate with Talent Engine to identify replacement React engineer by 30-Jun-2026 and implement cross-training for two backup team members on UI components.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If replacement is not secured by 15-Jul-2026, reallocate UI tasks to existing full-stack engineers and engage Ascendion tech manager to negotiate extended timeline with client for UI deliverables.

riskDescription.context: Go-green plan (04 Jun 2026) in EMS lists dependency on support from all leaders to groom resources and provide constructive feedback to strengthen quality deliverables. Biweekly CES Report (04 Jun 2026) notes need for support from AI execution and circle team to showcase AI strength.
riskDescription.condition: Leadership support and SME enablement may not be mobilized quickly enough or may not translate into visible client-facing demonstrations of AI capability.
riskDescription.consequence: Mitigation of RISK-802 could be delayed, prolonging Red CSAT status and increasing risk of client dissatisfaction and account impact.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Establish weekly SME office hours with AI execution and circle leaders to provide technical coaching and review offshore team deliverables before client presentation.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Should leadership support not materialize within two weeks, escalate to Circle Head Namratha A and deploy temporary onshore AI SME from practice pool to provide direct technical mentorship.

riskDescription.context: Biweekly CES Reports (28 May, 21 May 2026) in Project Artifacts document gap in alignment between vendors and gap in process understanding as cause of quality concerns. Dependency on alignment with customer and vendors to work as team is noted.
riskDescription.condition: Coordination between vendor teams may remain weak if process alignment and shared quality standards are not established and enforced.
riskDescription.consequence: Recurring misalignment could lead to continued code quality perception issues, impacting team morale and client confidence in multi-vendor delivery model.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Define and publish unified coding standards and dependency management protocol across all vendor teams with mandatory sign-off by 28-Jun-2026 and monthly compliance audits.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Once vendor misalignment causes sprint delay or client complaint, initiate tri-party governance meeting with client and all vendors within 48 hours to establish escalation path and assign single point of accountability.
